codeReview.summary: Implementation correctly covers all feature requirements: seed mode (50 entities), focus mode (?focus=:id), click-to-navigate, double-click-to-expand, drag-to-pin, pan/zoom, and all three states (loading/empty/error with retry). The code is well-structured with proper separation of concerns between ReactFlow state and force-layout graph state.

issues.description: Missing tests for core interaction behaviors: (1) click navigation - no test verifies navigate() is called with correct entity ID, (2) double-click expansion - no test verifies fetching relations and adding nodes, (3) drag pinning - no test verifies position is updated. These are the primary user-facing features but rely on ReactFlow event handlers which are difficult to test in isolation. Manual verification was performed via agent-browser which mitigates this gap.

useEntity and useEntityRelations are called with focusId ?? '' which results in calling with empty string when not in focus mode. While the hooks have enabled: !!id to prevent API calls, this is slightly wasteful. Consider using conditional hook calls or refactoring to avoid this pattern.

When expanding neighbors, duplicate edges could be added if the same relation exists in multiple expansion calls. The edge ID pattern `${fromId}-${toId}` is directional, so reverse relations would have different IDs, but if the API returns the same relation from different entity lookups, duplicates could occur. Consider deduplicating by edge ID before adding to graphEdges.

summary: PASS. The graph-page implementation is complete and correct. All feature requirements are met: seed mode with 50 entities, focus mode with URL parameter, click-to-navigate, double-click-to-expand, drag-to-pin, pan/zoom controls, and proper handling of loading/empty/error states with retry functionality. Test coverage has gaps for interaction behaviors but manual verification was thorough. No shared state updates needed.
